title: Majority Element II
description:
Return every value in nums that appears more than floor(nums.length / 3) times. Return the values in ascending order; if none qualify, return an empty list.

There can be at most two such values: three distinct values cannot each occupy over a third of the array. Pairing off groups of three different values narrows the candidates, but unlike the single-majority case, a final count is needed to verify them.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [3,2,3]
Output: [3]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,2]
Output: [1,2]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [1,2,3,4]
Output: []

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 50,000
  • -1,000,000,000 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000
  • Frequency must be strictly greater than floor(nums.length / 3), not equal to it.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The threshold is zero, so both values qualify.
Each value occurs once, which does not exceed floor(4 / 3).
